claims: Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces (FAR) consist of roughly 49,000 active-duty personnel.
FAR maintains a defensive doctrine known as the "war of the people".
FAR includes the Revolutionary Army, Revolutionary Navy, and Revolutionary Air and Air Defense Force.
FAR supported by paramilitary groups and a reserve force of approximately 39,000.
FAR has aging Soviet-era equipment.
FAR faces severe resource shortages.
FAR focuses on national mobilization and territorial defense rather than conventional power projection.
Revolutionary Army is the largest component of FAR.
Revolutionary Army focused on ground defense.
Revolutionary Navy responsible for coastal defense and maritime security.
Revolutionary Air and Air Defense Force operates a limited number of aging, mostly Soviet-era aircraft.
Cuba utilizes Territorial Troops Militia (MTT), Youth Labor Army (EJT), and Defense and Production Brigades to support the regular military.
Ministry of the Interior (MININT) operates Border Guard Troops and Special Troops.
Cuba’s primary military strategy is "War of the People" Doctrine.
"War of the People" Doctrine emphasizes the mobilization of the entire nation in the event of an existential threat or invasion.
"War of the People" Doctrine relies heavily on territorial defense and irregular warfare capabilities rather than large-scale conventional operations.
Cuban military has significantly decreased in size and capability since the end of the Cold War.
Cuban military decreased due to the loss of Soviet subsidies.
Cuban military hampered by chronic shortages of fuel, spare parts, and modernized technology.
Conventional fighting ability of Cuban military is considered limited.
Cuban government maintains a state of readiness for national defense and mobilization.
Cuban military remains a central institution within the Cuban state.
Cuban military has deep ties to the Communist Party and government leadership.
